title: Board-specific phases
description: I'm thinking that we may want to have board specific phases at some point; for example, I may just want to work on a plan but not actually implement anything; in that case, I would want to skip a bunch of phases.  Maybe allowing phases to be skipped would make sense, as a board configuration.
plan:
## What

Add a `terminal_stage` configuration option to per-board config that halts the automated pipeline waterfall after a named stage boundary. When the pipeline reaches the terminal stage boundary during an automated run, instead of continuing to the next block, items are routed to `final-human-approval` with a descriptive history entry. This enables boards to be scoped to specific purposes — e.g., a planning-only board that stops after plan review.

## Why

Different boards serve different purposes. A user may want a board purely for ideation and planning without ever generating specs or code. Currently, the pipeline is all-or-nothing: once an item enters the pipeline, it runs through every phase. A `terminal_stage` config gives boards clear boundaries that match their intended purpose, without requiring manual intervention to halt the pipeline at the desired point.

## Design

The mechanism is a single optional string field `terminal_stage` in the per-board config JSON file. Valid values correspond to the natural block boundaries in the pipeline: `"plan"` (stop after plan review passes) and `"spec"` (stop after spec review passes). When omitted, null, or empty string, the full pipeline runs as today (default behavior).

**Validation:** Invalid `terminal_stage` values (anything other than `"plan"`, `"spec"`, null, or omitted) should be detected when the config is read and logged as a warning. The pipeline should treat unrecognized values as if the field were omitted (full pipeline), rather than silently accepting typos like `"planning"` or numeric values. This fail-open approach avoids blocking the pipeline on config errors while still surfacing the misconfiguration.

**Guard mechanism at block boundaries:** After each major block completes successfully (plan review passes, spec review passes), the pipeline checks whether the board's `terminal_stage` matches that block. If so, the item is routed to `final-human-approval` with a history entry like "Terminal stage reached (plan) — moved to final-human-approval" and the pipeline returns.

**Critical bug fix (bundled):** The spec-writing block currently runs unconditionally after the plan review block exits. When `requires_human_approval` is true and plan review passes, the feature is moved to `awaiting-human-approval` and the review loop breaks, but execution falls through to the spec-writing block. An explicit stage guard must be added before the spec-writing block that checks whether the feature is still in a stage that warrants spec writing (i.e., `approved` stage). This guard is required for `terminal_stage` to work correctly and simultaneously fixes this pre-existing bug. The guard should check the feature's current stage — if the feature is not in `approved` stage when reaching the spec block, the pipeline should return without entering the spec block.

**Automated vs. manual moves:** The `terminal_stage` guard only applies within the automated pipeline orchestrator function. Manual stage moves (via CLI commands, TUI actions, or WebUI) go through a different code path that does not invoke the pipeline orchestrator. Therefore, no special detection mechanism is needed to distinguish automated from manual moves — the guard is structurally scoped to the orchestrator function. If a user manually moves an item past its board's terminal stage, the pipeline will not interfere because it is not running. If the auto-pipeline later picks up that item (now in a stage past the terminal boundary), it will process it from wherever it currently sits — the terminal_stage check only fires at block boundaries during a pipeline run, not retroactively.

**Items already in flight when terminal_stage is added:** When a board's `terminal_stage` is configured while items are already progressing through the pipeline, the behavior depends on where the item currently is relative to the terminal boundary:
- Items that have not yet reached the terminal boundary will stop at it on their next pipeline run — no issue.
- Items that have already passed the terminal boundary (e.g., already in `implementing` when `terminal_stage="plan"` is added) will continue through the remaining blocks normally. The guard checks occur at block boundaries during forward progression; since those items have already passed the relevant boundary, the guard won't fire. This is the correct behavior — retroactively halting in-flight work would be surprising and disruptive.
- Items currently in the middle of a block (e.g., in `spec-writing` when `terminal_stage="plan"` is set) will complete that block and then hit the guard at the next boundary. This is acceptable because partial block output (e.g., half-written specs) would be worse than completing the block.

**Items after reaching final-human-approval:** Items routed to `final-human-approval` by the terminal stage mechanism follow the same lifecycle as any other item in that stage. The human reviews the work product (plan, spec, etc.) and either approves it (moving to `done`) or rejects it (moving to `rejected`). This is existing behavior — no new handling is needed. The history entry should make it clear that the item reached final-human-approval due to the terminal stage configuration, not due to an error or review exhaustion.

## Impact

- Per-board config gains a new optional field; no existing configs are affected (field is optional with omitted meaning "run full pipeline")
- The pipeline orchestrator gains guard checks at two block boundaries — these are additive checks that don't change existing behavior when `terminal_stage` is not set
- The TUI and WebUI display items correctly since they already handle the `final-human-approval` stage
- The latent `requires_human_approval` fallthrough bug is fixed as a side effect of adding the stage guard before the spec-writing block
- The config loading infrastructure already supports per-board config — no new config plumbing is needed

## Risks

- Low overall risk: one new config field, a small number of targeted guard checks, and a bug fix
- The guard logic must correctly identify block boundaries — the two natural boundaries are after plan review and after spec review, which are clear in the code structure
- Config typos (e.g., `"planning"` instead of `"plan"`) could silently result in the full pipeline running. Mitigation: validation with warning logging when unrecognized values are encountered
- The bug fix (stage guard before spec block) changes control flow for the existing `requires_human_approval` case — this is intentional and correct, but should be tested to ensure no regression

## Scope

**In scope:**
- `terminal_stage` field in per-board config.json with `"plan"` and `"spec"` as valid values
- Guard checks at the two block boundaries in the pipeline orchestrator
- Stage guard before the ungated spec-writing block (fixes latent requires_human_approval fallthrough bug)
- Routing halted items to `final-human-approval` with descriptive history entries
- Validation/warning logging for invalid terminal_stage values

**Out of scope:**
- Skipping early phases (e.g., starting at planning without ideation)
- Per-feature terminal stage overrides
- UI changes beyond what already exists for `final-human-approval`
- Validation or migration tooling for board configs
- Retroactive enforcement on in-flight items that have already passed the terminal boundary

## Implementation Spec: Board-specific phases (terminal_stage)

### Task 1: Add `get_terminal_stage` method to `Config` class

**File:** `pipeline/config.py`

**What:** Add a method to `Config` that reads the `terminal_stage` field from a board's per-board config and validates it.

**Approach:**

1. Add a constant at module level (near line 36, after `PIPELINE_PHASES`):
   ```python
   VALID_TERMINAL_STAGES = {"plan", "spec"}
   ```

2. Add a method `get_terminal_stage(self, board_name: str) -> Optional[str]` to the `Config` class (after `_get_per_board_config`, around line 376):
   ```python
   def get_terminal_stage(self, board_name: str) -> Optional[str]:
       """Get the terminal_stage for a board, or None for full pipeline."""
       board_config = self._get_per_board_config(board_name)
       if not board_config:
           return None
       value = board_config.get("terminal_stage")
       if not value or not isinstance(value, str):
           return None
       value = value.strip().lower()
       if not value:
           return None
       if value not in VALID_TERMINAL_STAGES:
           logger.warning(
               f"Board '{board_name}' has invalid terminal_stage '{value}'. "
               f"Valid values: {VALID_TERMINAL_STAGES}. Running full pipeline."
           )
           return None
       return value
   ```

**Dependencies:** None. This is a standalone addition.

---

### Task 2: Add stage guard before spec-writing block (bug fix)

**File:** `pipeline/phases.py`

**What:** In `_run_pipeline_impl`, add a guard after the plan review block exits and before the spec-writing block begins. If the feature is not in `approved` stage at this point, return early. This fixes the latent bug where `requires_human_approval` causes the feature to move to `awaiting-human-approval` but execution falls through to spec writing.

**Approach:**

In `_run_pipeline_impl` (line 1552), after the plan review block (the `if feature.current_stage == "reviewing-plan":` block ending around line 1655), add a stage guard before line 1657 (`# Phase 1: Spec writing + spec review loop`):

```python
    # Stage guard: only proceed to spec writing if feature is in 'approved' stage.
    # This prevents fallthrough when requires_human_approval moved it to awaiting-human-approval,
    # or when terminal_stage halted the pipeline at the plan boundary.
    if feature.current_stage != "approved":
        logger.info(f"[pipeline] Feature '{feature.title}' is in '{feature.current_stage}', not 'approved'. Stopping pipeline.")
        return
```

This single guard fixes both:
- The pre-existing `requires_human_approval` fallthrough bug (feature is in `awaiting-human-approval`, not `approved`)
- The `terminal_stage="plan"` case (feature will be in `final-human-approval`, not `approved`)

**Dependencies:** None, but logically pairs with Task 3.

---

### Task 3: Add terminal_stage guard after plan review passes

**File:** `pipeline/phases.py`

**What:** After plan review passes and the feature is about to be promoted, check whether the board's `terminal_stage` is `"plan"`. If so, route to `final-human-approval` instead of `approved`/`awaiting-human-approval`.

**Approach:**

In `_run_pipeline_impl`, inside the plan review loop, after `verdict == "PASS"` is detected (around line 1600-1609), add the terminal_stage check. The modified block should be:

```python
            if verdict == "PASS":
                # Check terminal_stage before promoting
                config = Config()
                terminal_stage = config.get_terminal_stage(feature.board)
                if terminal_stage == "plan":
                    feature.move_to_stage("final-human-approval")
                    feature.add_history("TERMINAL_STAGE", "Terminal stage reached (plan) — moved to final-human-approval")
                    feature.save()
                    _git_commit(feature, "terminal stage reached (plan)")
                    console.print("[green]Plan approved. Terminal stage 'plan' reached — moved to final-human-approval.[/green]")
                    return
                elif feature.requires_human_approval:
                    feature.move_to_stage("awaiting-human-approval")
                    feature.add_history("AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL", "Plan approved by AI, awaiting human approval")
                else:
                    feature.move_to_stage("approved")
                    feature.add_history("PROMOTED", "Plan approved, moving to spec-writing")
                feature.save()
                _git_commit(feature, "plan approved")
                break
```

Note: The `terminal_stage` check goes BEFORE the `requires_human_approval` check because `terminal_stage` takes priority — if the board is configured to stop at plan, it should stop regardless of whether human approval is also configured.

**Dependencies:** Task 1 (needs `get_terminal_stage` method).

---

### Task 4: Add terminal_stage guard after spec review passes

**File:** `pipeline/phases.py`

**What:** After the spec review loop completes successfully (verdict == PASS), check whether the board's `terminal_stage` is `"spec"`. If so, route to `final-human-approval` instead of `implementing`.

**Approach:**

In `_run_pipeline_impl`, inside the spec review loop, after `verdict == "PASS"` (around line 1671-1676), modify to:

```python
        if verdict == "PASS":
            # Check terminal_stage before promoting to implementing
            config = Config()
            terminal_stage = config.get_terminal_stage(feature.board)
            if terminal_stage == "spec":
                feature.move_to_stage("final-human-approval")
                feature.add_history("TERMINAL_STAGE", "Terminal stage reached (spec) — moved to final-human-approval")
                feature.save()
                _git_commit(feature, "terminal stage reached (spec)")
                console.print("[green]Specs approved. Terminal stage 'spec' reached — moved to final-human-approval.[/green]")
                return
            feature.move_to_stage("implementing")
            feature.add_history("SPECREVIEW", "Specs approved, moving to implementing")
            feature.save()
            _git_commit(feature, "spec review passed")
            break
```

**Dependencies:** Task 1 (needs `get_terminal_stage` method).

---

### Task 5: Add unit tests

**File:** `pipeline/test_phases_unit.py` (existing test file)

**What:** Add tests covering:
1. `Config.get_terminal_stage` returns correct values for valid configs
2. `Config.get_terminal_stage` returns None and logs warning for invalid values
3. `Config.get_terminal_stage` returns None when field is omitted/null/empty
4. Pipeline stops at plan boundary when `terminal_stage="plan"`
5. Pipeline stops at spec boundary when `terminal_stage="spec"`
6. Pipeline runs full when `terminal_stage` is not set (no regression)
7. Stage guard before spec-writing prevents fallthrough when feature is in `awaiting-human-approval` (bug fix test)

**Approach:**

For the config tests, create temporary board config files with various `terminal_stage` values and assert the return values of `get_terminal_stage()`.

For the pipeline tests, mock the relevant phase functions and verify that `_run_pipeline_impl` stops at the correct point based on `terminal_stage` configuration. Use `unittest.mock.patch` to mock `Config.get_terminal_stage` to return the desired value.

Key test cases:
- `test_terminal_stage_plan_stops_after_plan_review`: Set `terminal_stage="plan"`, mock plan review to return PASS, verify feature ends up in `final-human-approval` and spec writing is never called.
- `test_terminal_stage_spec_stops_after_spec_review`: Set `terminal_stage="spec"`, mock plan+spec review to return PASS, verify feature ends up in `final-human-approval` and implementing is never called.
- `test_terminal_stage_none_runs_full_pipeline`: No terminal_stage set, verify full pipeline runs.
- `test_stage_guard_prevents_spec_fallthrough`: Set `requires_human_approval=True`, mock plan review to PASS, verify spec writing is NOT called (feature is in `awaiting-human-approval`).
- `test_get_terminal_stage_valid_values`: Test that "plan" and "spec" are returned correctly.
- `test_get_terminal_stage_invalid_value_warns`: Test that "planning", "implement", 123, etc. return None and log a warning.
- `test_get_terminal_stage_missing_returns_none`: Test omitted, null, empty string all return None.

**Dependencies:** Tasks 1-4.

---

### Summary of files modified:
- `pipeline/config.py` — add `VALID_TERMINAL_STAGES` constant and `get_terminal_stage()` method
- `pipeline/phases.py` — add stage guard before spec block, add terminal_stage checks at plan and spec boundaries in `_run_pipeline_impl`
- `pipeline/test_phases_unit.py` — add unit tests

### Execution order:
1. Task 1 (config method) — no dependencies
2. Task 2 (stage guard / bug fix) — no dependencies
3. Task 3 (plan boundary guard) — depends on Task 1
4. Task 4 (spec boundary guard) — depends on Task 1
5. Task 5 (tests) — depends on Tasks 1-4
test_spec:
# Test Specification: Board-specific phases (terminal_stage)

## 1. Behaviors That MUST Be Verified

### 1.1 Config: get_terminal_stage returns valid values

**Behavior:** When a board's per-board config.json contains `"terminal_stage": "plan"`, calling `Config.get_terminal_stage(board_name)` returns `"plan"`. Same for `"spec"`.

**Success criteria:** Method returns the exact string `"plan"` or `"spec"` respectively.

**Expected output:** `"plan"` when config has `"terminal_stage": "plan"`, `"spec"` when config has `"terminal_stage": "spec"`.

---

### 1.2 Config: get_terminal_stage returns None when field is absent

**Behavior:** When a board's per-board config.json does not contain the `terminal_stage` field at all, `get_terminal_stage` returns `None`.

**Success criteria:** Method returns `None`.

**Expected output:** `None`.

---

### 1.3 Config: get_terminal_stage returns None for null value

**Behavior:** When a board's per-board config.json has `"terminal_stage": null`, `get_terminal_stage` returns `None`.

**Success criteria:** Method returns `None`.

**Expected output:** `None`.

---

### 1.4 Config: get_terminal_stage returns None for empty string

**Behavior:** When a board's per-board config.json has `"terminal_stage": ""`, `get_terminal_stage` returns `None`.

**Success criteria:** Method returns `None`.

**Expected output:** `None`.

---

### 1.5 Config: get_terminal_stage logs warning for invalid values

**Behavior:** When a board's per-board config.json has `"terminal_stage": "planning"` (or any other unrecognized string like `"implement"`, `"full"`, `"test"`), `get_terminal_stage` returns `None` AND logs a warning message that includes the invalid value and the set of valid values.

**Success criteria:** Method returns `None`. A warning log message is emitted containing the invalid value string and mentioning the valid options.

**Expected output:** `None` return value. Warning log contains `"planning"` (or whichever invalid value was used) and mentions `"plan"` and `"spec"` as valid.

---

### 1.6 Config: get_terminal_stage returns None for non-string values

**Behavior:** When a board's per-board config.json has `"terminal_stage": 123` or `"terminal_stage": true` or `"terminal_stage": ["plan"]`, `get_terminal_stage` returns `None` without crashing.

**Success criteria:** Method returns `None` gracefully (no exception raised).

**Expected output:** `None`.

---

### 1.7 Config: get_terminal_stage handles missing board config

**Behavior:** When there is no per-board config.json file for the given board name, `get_terminal_stage` returns `None`.

**Success criteria:** Method returns `None` without error.

**Expected output:** `None`.

---

### 1.8 Pipeline: terminal_stage="plan" stops after plan review passes

**Behavior:** When `terminal_stage` is `"plan"` for the feature's board, and plan review returns PASS, the pipeline moves the feature to `final-human-approval` and returns without entering the spec-writing block.

**Success criteria:**
- Feature ends up in stage `final-human-approval`
- Feature history contains an entry with tag `TERMINAL_STAGE` and a message mentioning `"plan"` and `"final-human-approval"`
- `run_spec_writing` is never called
- `run_implementing` is never called
- Pipeline function returns normally (no exception)

**Expected output:** Feature in `final-human-approval` stage with appropriate history entry.

---

### 1.9 Pipeline: terminal_stage="spec" stops after spec review passes

**Behavior:** When `terminal_stage` is `"spec"` for the feature's board, plan review passes, spec writing runs, spec review returns PASS, the pipeline moves the feature to `final-human-approval` and returns without entering the implementing block.

**Success criteria:**
- Feature ends up in stage `final-human-approval`
- Feature history contains an entry with tag `TERMINAL_STAGE` and a message mentioning `"spec"` and `"final-human-approval"`
- `run_spec_writing` IS called (specs are still written)
- `run_implementing` is never called
- Pipeline function returns normally

**Expected output:** Feature in `final-human-approval` stage with appropriate history entry.

---

### 1.10 Pipeline: no terminal_stage runs full pipeline (regression test)

**Behavior:** When `terminal_stage` is not set (or is None) for the feature's board, the pipeline runs through all phases as before: planning, plan review, spec writing, spec review, implementing, testing, review.

**Success criteria:**
- All pipeline phases are invoked in order
- Feature progresses through all expected stages
- No `TERMINAL_STAGE` history entries appear
- Final outcome is the same as the current pipeline behavior

**Expected output:** Full pipeline execution identical to current behavior.

---

### 1.11 Pipeline: stage guard before spec-writing prevents fallthrough (bug fix)

**Behavior:** When `requires_human_approval` is `True` on a feature, and plan review returns PASS, the feature is moved to `awaiting-human-approval`. The pipeline must NOT proceed to spec writing. It should return without entering the spec-writing block.

**Success criteria:**
- Feature ends up in `awaiting-human-approval` stage
- `run_spec_writing` is never called
- Pipeline returns normally

**Expected output:** Feature in `awaiting-human-approval`, no spec writing executed.

---

### 1.12 Pipeline: terminal_stage="plan" takes priority over requires_human_approval

**Behavior:** When both `terminal_stage="plan"` and `requires_human_approval=True` are set, and plan review passes, the terminal_stage check fires first and the feature goes to `final-human-approval` (not `awaiting-human-approval`).

**Success criteria:**
- Feature ends up in `final-human-approval` (not `awaiting-human-approval`)
- History entry is the terminal_stage entry, not the human approval entry

**Expected output:** Feature in `final-human-approval` with `TERMINAL_STAGE` history.

---

### 1.13 Pipeline: terminal_stage="spec" allows plan review to proceed normally

**Behavior:** When `terminal_stage="spec"`, the plan review block runs completely normally (including retries on FAIL, re-planning, etc.). The terminal_stage guard only fires after spec review passes, not at the plan boundary.

**Success criteria:**
- Plan review loop behaves identically to the no-terminal-stage case
- Feature progresses through planning, plan review, approved, spec writing, spec review
- After spec review PASS, feature goes to `final-human-approval`

**Expected output:** Normal plan review behavior, then halt at spec boundary.

---

### 1.14 History entries: terminal stage entries are descriptive

**Behavior:** When the terminal stage guard fires, the history entry clearly states the reason (terminal stage configuration) and which boundary was reached.

**Success criteria:**
- History entry tag is `TERMINAL_STAGE`
- History note contains the terminal stage value (e.g., `"plan"` or `"spec"`)
- History note contains `"final-human-approval"`
- The entry is distinguishable from review-exhaustion entries and error entries

**Expected output:** History entry like `"Terminal stage reached (plan) — moved to final-human-approval"`.

---

### 1.15 Config: case insensitivity for terminal_stage values

**Behavior:** The `get_terminal_stage` method normalizes the value to lowercase, so `"Plan"`, `"PLAN"`, `"Plan"` all return `"plan"`.

**Success criteria:** All case variations of `"plan"` and `"spec"` return the lowercase version.

**Expected output:** `"plan"` for `"Plan"`, `"PLAN"`, etc. `"spec"` for `"Spec"`, `"SPEC"`, etc.

---

### 1.16 Config: whitespace handling for terminal_stage values

**Behavior:** The `get_terminal_stage` method strips whitespace, so `" plan "` returns `"plan"`.

**Success criteria:** Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped before validation.

**Expected output:** `"plan"` for `" plan "`, `"spec"` for `" spec "`.

---

## 2. Edge Cases

### 2.1 Plan review fails all retries with terminal_stage="plan"

**Behavior:** When `terminal_stage="plan"` and plan review fails all retry attempts, the existing exhaustion logic should still apply — the feature goes to `final-human-approval` via the existing exhaustion path, not via the terminal stage guard.

**Success criteria:** Feature ends up in `final-human-approval` via the review-exhaustion path. The terminal_stage guard never fires (because plan review never passed).

**Expected output:** Feature in `final-human-approval` with review exhaustion history entry (not terminal stage entry).

---

### 2.2 Spec review fails all retries with terminal_stage="spec"

**Behavior:** When `terminal_stage="spec"` and spec review fails all retry attempts, the existing graceful degradation logic should apply — specs proceed to implementing anyway. The terminal_stage guard does NOT fire because spec review did not pass.

**Success criteria:** Feature proceeds to implementing (existing behavior when spec review is exhausted). The terminal_stage guard does not fire.

**Expected output:** Feature moves to implementing via existing exhaustion logic.

---

### 2.3 Feature already past terminal boundary when pipeline runs

**Behavior:** If a feature is already in `implementing` stage and the board has `terminal_stage="plan"`, running the pipeline (e.g., via `run_pipeline_from_implementing`) should process the feature normally through implement/test/review. The terminal_stage guard only fires at block boundaries during forward progression; it should not retroactively halt items.

**Success criteria:** Feature progresses through implementing, testing, and review normally. No terminal stage halt.

**Expected output:** Normal implement/test/review loop execution.

---

### 2.4 Feature in approved stage with terminal_stage="plan"

**Behavior:** If a feature has already been moved to `approved` stage (past the plan boundary) and the board has `terminal_stage="plan"`, running `run_pipeline` should enter the spec-writing block because the feature is in `approved`. The terminal_stage="plan" guard only fires within the plan review block when plan review passes.

**Success criteria:** Feature enters spec writing and continues normally. The terminal_stage guard does not fire retroactively.

**Expected output:** Normal pipeline progression from approved through specs and implementation.

---

### 2.5 Board config file is malformed JSON

**Behavior:** If the per-board config.json is malformed (not valid JSON), `_get_per_board_config` already returns `None`, so `get_terminal_stage` should return `None` without crashing.

**Success criteria:** `get_terminal_stage` returns `None`. No unhandled exception. Pipeline runs full.

**Expected output:** `None`, full pipeline execution.

---

### 2.6 Board config file has extra unexpected fields

**Behavior:** If the per-board config.json has `terminal_stage` alongside other unknown fields, `get_terminal_stage` should still correctly read the `terminal_stage` field and ignore others.

**Success criteria:** `terminal_stage` is read correctly. Extra fields do not interfere.

**Expected output:** Correct `terminal_stage` value returned.

---

### 2.7 terminal_stage with whitespace-only value

**Behavior:** If `terminal_stage` is set to `"   "` (whitespace only), after stripping it becomes empty string, so `get_terminal_stage` should return `None`.

**Success criteria:** Returns `None`.

**Expected output:** `None`.

---

### 2.8 Pipeline called for feature on board without per-board config

**Behavior:** When the feature's board has no per-board config.json at all (the default case for most boards), `get_terminal_stage` returns `None` and the pipeline runs the full waterfall.

**Success criteria:** No errors. Full pipeline runs.

**Expected output:** Full pipeline execution.

---

### 2.9 Stage guard with feature in reviewing-plan (neither approved nor awaiting-human-approval)

**Behavior:** If for some reason the feature is still in `reviewing-plan` when execution reaches the stage guard before spec writing (this could happen if plan review logic changes), the guard should prevent spec writing from running.

**Success criteria:** Feature does not enter spec writing. Pipeline returns.

**Expected output:** Pipeline returns without entering spec block.

---

### 2.10 terminal_stage="plan" with questions during planning

**Behavior:** When `terminal_stage="plan"` and the planning phase raises questions (moving feature to `requested-input`), the pipeline should pause as normal. The terminal_stage only fires when plan review actually passes, not during the planning loop.

**Success criteria:** Feature moves to `requested-input` as normal. Pipeline returns waiting for human input. Terminal stage guard does not fire.

**Expected output:** Feature in `requested-input`, pipeline paused.

---

## 3. What Constitutes Failure

### 3.1 Config failures

- `get_terminal_stage` raises an unhandled exception for any input (including None board name, missing config, malformed JSON, non-string values, numeric values, boolean values, array values)
- `get_terminal_stage` returns a non-None value for invalid terminal_stage strings (e.g., returns `"planning"` instead of `None`)
- `get_terminal_stage` returns a non-None value when the field is absent, null, or empty string
- No warning is logged when an invalid (non-empty, non-null) terminal_stage value is provided
- Warning log message does not include the invalid value or valid options

### 3.2 Pipeline guard failures

- Feature enters spec-writing when `terminal_stage="plan"` and plan review passed — the terminal stage guard failed to fire
- Feature enters implementing when `terminal_stage="spec"` and spec review passed — the terminal stage guard failed to fire
- Feature does NOT enter spec-writing when `terminal_stage` is not set and plan review passed — false positive guard activation
- Feature ends up in a stage other than `final-human-approval` when a terminal stage guard fires (e.g., `done`, `approved`, `rejected`)
- Pipeline raises an unhandled exception when terminal stage guard fires
- No history entry is added when the terminal stage guard fires
- History entry tag is not `TERMINAL_STAGE` or does not mention the boundary name

### 3.3 Bug fix failures

- Feature enters spec-writing when `requires_human_approval=True` and plan review passed — the stage guard before spec block is missing or broken (this is the pre-existing bug)
- Feature enters spec-writing when it is in any stage other than `approved` after the plan review block completes

### 3.4 Regression failures

- Full pipeline behavior changes when `terminal_stage` is not configured — any difference from current behavior when the field is absent
- Plan review retry logic is altered — retries, re-planning, system error handling should be unchanged
- Spec review retry logic is altered — retries, graceful degradation should be unchanged
- The implement/test/review loop is altered — retry count, feedback handling should be unchanged
- Features that have already passed a terminal boundary are retroactively halted

### 3.5 Error messages expected

- Warning log: When invalid terminal_stage value is encountered, a warning containing the invalid value and valid options should be logged
- Info log: When the stage guard before spec-writing fires, an info-level log should indicate the feature's current stage and that the pipeline is stopping

## 4. Out of Scope

- **UI testing:** No testing of TUI or WebUI rendering of items in `final-human-approval` — these already work.
- **Visual assertions:** No screenshot or visual comparison testing.
- **Performance benchmarks:** No timing tests for how fast the terminal stage check executes.
- **Manual stage move testing:** The terminal_stage guard only applies within the automated pipeline orchestrator. Manual moves via CLI/TUI/WebUI use different code paths and do not need testing for this feature.
- **Per-feature terminal stage overrides:** Out of scope per the plan.
- **Skipping early phases:** Starting at planning without ideation is explicitly out of scope.
- **Config migration tooling:** No testing of config migration or validation tooling for board configs.
- **End-to-end agent execution:** Tests should mock the agent runner; no real AI agent calls.
- **Concurrent pipeline execution:** The pipeline uses a lock mechanism; concurrent runs are prevented by the lock, not by terminal_stage logic.
- **Network/filesystem error handling during config reads:** The existing `_get_per_board_config` already handles these; no new error paths are introduced.
- **Testing the `run_pipeline_from_implementing` entry point with terminal_stage:** This entry point skips planning and spec writing entirely, so terminal stage guards at those boundaries are structurally unreachable. No special testing needed.

Ideation:
Board-specific phases would let individual boards opt out of pipeline stages they don't need — a planning-only board stops after plan review, a board without ideation skips to planning. After multiple debate cycles, the discussion has firmly converged on `terminal_stage` as the right mechanism: a single board config field that halts the pipeline waterfall after a named stage and routes items to `final-human-approval` rather than auto-closing them. This preserves the human checkpoint while delivering the highest-value use case (plan-only boards) with minimal code risk. The competing `active_phases` approach — a unified list declaring which of the three natural sub-pipeline blocks run — was rejected because it reintroduces the data contract problem: skipping spec-writing while keeping impl leaves `impl_spec` and `test_spec` empty, producing garbage output from the implementing phase.

The critical implementation subtlety identified in this cycle is that the spec-writing block (~line 1657 in `_run_pipeline_impl`) has no stage guard and runs unconditionally after the plan review block completes. A `terminal_stage='plan'` configuration cannot simply skip entering the spec block — it requires an explicit check before that ungated block. This is not a novel design challenge but it must be addressed in the implementation. More importantly, round 4 of this cycle revealed that this same structural gap already constitutes a latent bug: when `requires_human_approval` is true and plan review passes, the feature is moved to `awaiting-human-approval` and the for-loop breaks, but execution falls through to the spec-writing block which then runs unconditionally against an item that is no longer in the expected pipeline state. The `terminal_stage` fix — adding an explicit guard before the ungated spec block — would simultaneously resolve this pre-existing bug.

The design is now well-understood: add `terminal_stage` to board config (loaded via `_get_per_board_config`), check it at each block boundary in `_run_pipeline_impl`, add an explicit guard before the ungated spec-writing block (fixing both `terminal_stage` and the latent `requires_human_approval` fallthrough), and route halted items to `final-human-approval`. Skipping early phases (e.g., starting directly at planning without ideation) remains out of scope — it requires either pre-populating data fields or formalizing sub-pipeline data contracts, both non-trivial follow-on efforts. The overall risk is low: one new config field, a small number of targeted guard checks, and a bug fix bundled into the same change.

[Ideation concluded by consensus after 4 rounds, 1 cycles.]

plan_exploration_summary:
Explored the MAD pipeline codebase to understand the architecture for board-specific phases.

Files examined:
- pipeline/phases.py: Contains _run_pipeline_impl (the main orchestrator), run_spec_writing, run_plan_review, run_spec_review, _run_impl_test_review_loop. The orchestrator has three sequential blocks: (1) planning + plan review, (2) spec writing + spec review, (3) implement/test/review. Confirmed the latent bug: after plan review passes with requires_human_approval=true, feature is moved to awaiting-human-approval and the for-loop breaks, but execution falls through unconditionally to Phase 1 (spec writing) at line 1657 with no stage guard.
- pipeline/config.py: Config class with _get_per_board_config(board_name) method that loads per-board config.json from boards_dir/<board>/config.json. Currently used for code_path lookups. The infrastructure for reading per-board config already exists.
- pipeline/state.py: STAGES list defines all valid stages including final-human-approval. FeatureFile.move_to_stage validates against STAGES. The board property is available on FeatureFile.
- pipeline/pipeline.py: CLI entry points including run, auto, and the edit-feature command.
- config.json (root): Global config with boards list, agent configuration.

Key architecture insights:
- Per-board config infrastructure already exists via _get_per_board_config which loads JSON from the board directory
- The pipeline orchestrator (_run_pipeline_impl) uses sequential if-blocks for each phase, not a state machine — block boundaries are implicit code locations, not declarative
- Features know their board (feature.board property) which can be used to look up board config
- The spec-writing block (Phase 1, line 1657) has no guard checking whether the feature is still in an appropriate stage — it runs unconditionally after the plan review block exits, regardless of whether the feature was moved to awaiting-human-approval
- Manual stage moves happen via move_to_stage on FeatureFile, which is also what the automated pipeline uses — there is no flag distinguishing automated from manual moves
- Items in final-human-approval are already a well-established pattern — items land there when reviews exhaust retries or when the full pipeline completes successfully

Existing patterns found:
- The requires_human_approval flag on features provides a precedent for per-feature pipeline behavior modification
- Guard-style checks already exist (e.g., checking feature.current_stage before entering planning block)
- _get_per_board_config returns Optional[dict] and is already called in property accessors

Edge cases in section 2 (review exhaustion, feature past boundary, malformed JSON) are handled by existing error handling and integration scenarios.
